Visit note | 2025-04-03 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Rupa Mondal, 72, female. Mrs. Mondal presents for her first visit complaining of a burning sensation in both feet that feels worse at night. She mentions that this became more noticeable after she walked barefoot at home in Mymensingh. She works as a homemaker and has no significant comorbidities. On examination: BP 117/84 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 59 kg, with reduced sensation noted at 8 of 10 monofilament test sites. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-04-05 09:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Zakia Ahmed, 38, female. Mrs. Ahmed attends her initial consultation stating she is constantly thirsty and needs to pass urine frequently. She explains that her sugar readings rose during a busy work season as a hotel receptionist in Jashore. She has no known comorbidities. On examination: BP 130/83 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 62 kg, and fasting glucose is 9.1 mmol/L. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly for 30 minutes five days a week, check her fasting sugar twice weekly, and check her feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.
